name: Baladan
title: Father of Merodach-Baladan, king of Babylon
summary: Baladan is known from the Bible as the father of Merodach-Baladan (also called Berodach-Baladan), king of Babylon. He is mentioned in connection with Merodach-Baladan's envoys to King Hezekiah of Judah. Although little is known about Baladan personally, his son is an important historical figure in the relationship between Babylon and Judah.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as father of Merodach-Baladan in 2 Kings
keyEvents.description: Baladan is identified as the father of Berodach-Baladan, king of Babylon, who sent letters and gifts to King Hezekiah when he was ill.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as father of Merodach-Baladan in Isaiah
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah mentions Baladan as the father of Merodach-Baladan, king of Babel, in connection with the Babylonian delegation's visit to Hezekiah.

keyEvents.title: Merodach-Baladan's envoys to Hezekiah
keyEvents.description: Baladan's son Merodach-Baladan sent envoys with letters and gifts to Hezekiah after his illness. This visit had great consequences when Hezekiah showed them all his treasures.

keyEvents.title: Isaiah's prophecy about the Babylonian exile
keyEvents.description: After the visit of Merodach-Baladan's envoys, Isaiah prophesied that everything in Hezekiah's palace would one day be carried off to Babylon, a consequence linked to Baladan's dynasty's connection with Judah.
